transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lucia Gomez (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (Equinox - Head of MLOps), Maya Rios (Equinox - Infra), Tom Haines (Equinox - CISO)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs, isolation/VPC needs, burst strategy, autoscaling expectations, and security requirements (SOC2/KMS). Agreed to run an initial benchmark using Equinox's model suite, Redwood to send pricing and SOW.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:06] Jared (Equinox): Jared here, run the MLOps team. we own model infra, latency is... well a big thing for us.
[00:10] Maya (Equinox): Maya, infra manager, security and network questions i have later.
[00:14] Tom (Equinox): Tom, CISO. i'll be listening for compliance, KMS, logs.
[00:18] Lucia (Redwood): Lucia here, SE. i'll dig into performance and the benchmark plan.
[00:25] Samir: Great. quick context - why dedicated? Jared?
[00:29] Jared: So we're moving from cloud-hosted endpoints to a reserved capacity model because of predictable cost and data isolation. We process credit decisioning models, PII in payloads, and need strict network isolation. latency target is P95 < 250ms for our 512-token prompts for the customer-facing flow.
[00:45] Samir: Ok. good. what about throughput? qps or concurrent users?
[00:49] Jared: Peak is about 120 QPS across 3 regions, but typical steady state is 20-30 QPS. Burst windows can go up to 300 QPS for a few minutes during batch releases.
[01:03] Lucia: That burst pattern is common; we support burst through spare pool and autoscale. with Dedicated you pick a reserved GPU pool and configure burst nodes. question: are you expecting zero noisy-neighbor exposure?
[01:15] Maya: Yes, isolation is required. we need dedicated tenancy, no co-tenant VMs, and control plane access through our VPC peering. also want to use our KMS for keys.
[01:28] Tom: SOC 2 is a must and we need audit logs for all inference traffic. can you provide details?
[01:34] Samir: Absolutely. our Dedicated offering includes customer-dedicated GPU pools and VPC peering for control/data plane. we support KMS integrations (bring-your-own KMS) and provide audit logs — i'll send SOC2 and technical deployment docs after call.
[01:47] Jared: Good. on models - we're using several Llama-3 variants and a couple of in-house distilled models. quantized runs are important to save cost. what's your support for quantization and kernel selection?
[02:01] Lucia: We do kernel selection and quantization-friendly execution paths in the runtime. for Llama-3 we recommend the 4-bit quant profiles we tested; latency regresses slightly but cost drops ~40%. We'll validate against your models in the benchmark. note: sometimes transcriptions call it the "quantize" path, but it's quantization.
[02:20] Maya: Network topology — we require private control plane in our VPC and egress restrictions. can you do on-prem or air-gapped?
[02:28] Samir: We have a Private offering for full on-prem or VPC with a private control plane. For Dedicated, we can do VPC peering + private endpoints and ensure no public egress for inference data. On-prem is possible but will be scoped separately.
[02:41] Tom: Encryption at rest and in transit? plus HSM?
[02:44] Lucia: TLS for transit, and at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). We also provide configurable retention windows for logs and ability to redact some fields.
[02:55] Jared: Operationally, how do rollouts work? we want canaries and fallback to hosted if a model regresses.
[03:00] Samir: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted pool if dedicated capacity is saturated. you can set policies by route.
[03:12] Maya: Autoscaling policy details? we need predictable cold starts.
[03:15] Lucia: Autoscale can be configured with warm standby nodes and burst capacity. warm standbys keep some GPUs hot to avoid cold-start latency. you can set scale thresholds by P95 latency or queue depth.
[03:28] Jared: Pricing behavior during burst? we prefer a committed monthly with burst overage rates rather than ephemeral costly nodes.
[03:34] Samir: We typically do committed monthly tiers plus defined burst buckets. burst overage is cheaper than immediate on-demand cloud GPUs because we reserve capacity in our pool. we'll send a sample pricing grid.
[03:46] Tom: Any multi-region replication for failover?
[03:49] Lucia: Yes, you can configure cross-region replication and automatic failover. keep in mind model sync times for large weights if you're on-prem.
[03:57] Jared: For benchmarks, we want to test: 1) P95 latency at 512 tokens, 2) throughput at 120 QPS sustained for 10 minutes, 3) cold-start times, 4) quantized vs full-precision accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
[04:12] Lucia: perfect. we'll need sample prompts, model binaries or repo access for the distilled models, QPS profile, and network egress rules.
[04:21] Jared: i'll get that to you. likely a list of 4 models and sample traffic generator configs.
[04:25] Samir: on security, i'll include our SOC 2 summary, VPC peering diagram, KMS integration steps, and retention defaults. any legal/contractual constraints?
[04:33] Tom: Data residency — must keep logs in region and have retention windows. also need SAML SSO and RBAC integration.
[04:40] Samir: we support region-restricted logs, SAML, and RBAC. we'll include details in the doc.
[04:46] Maya: curious about KV cache, prefix caching. do you do prefix/KV caching to reduce token costs for system prompts?
[04:52] Lucia: yes, we support prefix and KV caching at the runtime layer to reduce repeated prefix costs. caching rules can be per-route. sometimes our transcriptions show "KV cash" lol but it's cache.
[05:03] Jared: Great. what's expected lead time to provision a Dedicated pool?
[05:07] Samir: for standard configs it's 2-4 weeks after contract signature. with custom network/VPC peering and KMS it can be 4-8 weeks. for on-prem it's longer and scoped separately.
[05:18] Maya: Do you provide monitoring hooks we can ingest into our Prometheus/Grafana?
[05:22] Lucia: yes, we expose metrics, traces, and per-token cost breakdowns. you can send to your observability stack or use Redwood Console.
[05:31] Jared: Compliance question — can we run a pen test against the Dedicated environment?
[05:34] Tom: yes, we usually require that for vendor onboarding.
[05:36] Samir: We have a pen test process and can share the scope. we'll coordinate with your security team.
[05:41] Jared: On model updates — how do you handle KV cache invalidation when we deploy a new model?
[05:46] Lucia: You can flush caches per-route or let the runtime maintain versioned caches. if model architecture changes significantly, we recommend cache flush on deploy.
[05:55] Maya: Any constraints on model size or sharding?
[05:58] Lucia: We support multi-GPU sharded models and have recommendations on sequence length and batch sizing. for very large models we do model parallelism; we'll include guidance in the benchmark plan.
[06:09] Jared: Ok, sounds good. what's our next step timeline?
[06:12] Samir: We'll send: pricing + SOW, SOC2 + deployment docs, and a benchmark plan. we'd like to run the benchmark mid-March.
[06:20] Jared: i'll share model artifacts and QPS profile by Mar 11.
[06:24] Tom: we'll review the SOC2 and legal; may want a security questionnaire.
[06:28] Samir: we'll attach our standard security questionnaire and answers.
[06:31] Maya: one more question — what's your fallback behavior during saturation? you mentioned host fallback, but if the hosted service is down?
[06:37] Lucia: you can configure multi-tier fallbacks: first fallback to another dedicated pool in a secondary region, then to our hosted pool. if hosted is down we'll fallback to a smaller local queue with degraded throughput but preserved correctness.
[06:50] Jared: sounds reasonable.
[06:53] Samir: ok i'll recap next steps.
[06:55] Samir: Next steps recap: 1) Redwood send pricing + SOW and SOC2 docs (Samir) 2) Redwood send benchmark plan and request list (Lucia) 3) Equinox provide models, prompts, QPS by 2026-03-11 (Jared) 4) Schedule benchmark week of 2026-03-15.
[07:15] Tom: good. thanks everyone.
[07:18] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

Note: timestamps above are periodic markers; full call had more back-and-forth and occasional crosstalk. Some product names transcribed imperfectly in the call.
